results.corrected_title: Epoch AI: open-weight models are about 6-7 months behind closed models on cyber capabilities
results.corrected_summary: On 16 October 2026 Epoch AI published an analysis of its Cyber ECI index, using data up to 8 October. It found that the best open-weight model, Z.ai's GLM-5.3 (score 160), sits roughly where the closed frontier stood 6-7 months earlier. GLM-5.3 beats OpenAI's GPT-5.4 from March 2026 but trails Claude Mythos Preview and GPT-5.5 from April 2026, and the current closed leaders, Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra, score 171. Separately, on 14 October Epoch launched the SpireClimb benchmark: frontier models now win Slay the Spire 1 at the easiest level at least 90% of the time, and the best model wins about 20% at the hardest level.
key_facts: Published 16 Oct 2026 by Jaeho Lee and Alexander Barry; data as of 8 Oct 2026
Top open-weight model on Cyber ECI is Z.ai GLM-5.3, score 160 (90% interval 155.8-167.0)
Closed frontier: Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra both score 171
October update expanded the index from 56 to 76 models and from 20 to 35 cyber benchmarks
SpireClimb (14 Oct): at Ascension 0, GPT-6 Astra wins 98% and Claude Opus 5.5 93%; at Ascension 20 Heart, GPT-6.1 Sol wins 20% and GPT-6 Astra 17%
Epoch notes that these win rates remain far below top human players
results.issues: Mostly accurate. 'Leading models win >90%' holds only for top frontier models: Claude Sonnet 5.5 wins 83% and GPT-6 Luna 25% at Ascension 0. '~20% on hardest' is the best single model (GPT-6.1 Sol); most models score 0-2%. These are two separate Epoch publications (14 and 16 Oct), both inside the window.

results.corrected_title: Sferical One formally launched in Stockholm: Swedish industrial groups share an AI supercomputer, opened with Jensen Huang
results.corrected_summary: On 15 October 2026 Sferical AI formally launched Sferical One in Stockholm, with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang present. Sferical AI is a jointly owned venture of AstraZeneca, Ericsson, Saab, SEB and Wallenberg Investments, with SKF as a strategic partner since April 2026. The machine has 1,152 Nvidia Blackwell Ultra GPUs in 16 DGX GB300 NVL72 racks and has been running since late summer 2026. During the visit Huang said Nvidia had invested $8 billion in Europe over the past year; on the same day Nvidia and the Norrsken Foundation announced a Stockholm AI Lab opening in 2027, and Volvo Cars said it is expanding its Nvidia partnership.
key_facts: Formal launch on Thursday 15 Oct 2026 in Stockholm; system running since late summer 2026
Owners: AstraZeneca, Ericsson, Saab, SEB, Wallenberg Investments; SKF strategic partner since April 2026; CEO Jenny Nordlöw
1,152 Nvidia Blackwell Ultra GPUs in 16 DGX GB300 NVL72 racks across two DGX SuperPODs
Huang: 'In the last one year, we've invested $8 billion already' in Europe, with 'another couple of billion dollars in the pipeline'
Nvidia and Norrsken Foundation will open the Stockholm AI Lab (Birger Jarlsgatan 37) in 2027
Volvo Cars is expanding its Nvidia partnership for safety technology in its planned self-driving cars
results.issues: Ownership and GPU details come only from Tech Times, which is inconsistent about the partner count. Owner-level details are therefore medium-confidence. The AFP article confirms the Huang quotes, the $8bn figure and Volvo, but not the GPU details. Sferical AI was incorporated in August 2025 and the system was already running before the window, so the new event is only the formal launch on 15 Oct. The headline 'sovereign' is Tech Times' framing.

results.corrected_title: Hogan Lovells Cadwalader rolls out Legora globally, capping a week of Legora launches
results.corrected_summary: On 16 October 2026 Hogan Lovells Cadwalader announced a global rollout of the legal AI platform Legora to its more than 3,300 lawyers in over 36 offices, after a pilot with more than 1,300 lawyers across 18 practice teams. Earlier that week, on 13 October, Legora launched Intake, an agentic 'front door' for in-house legal teams that starts in Slack, and announced a time-capture partnership with Laurel. On 14 October it launched an ecosystem of more than 30 integrations, including a partnership with contract-management firm Sirion.
key_facts: 16 Oct 2026: Hogan Lovells Cadwalader (formed in 2026 from the merger of Hogan Lovells and Cadwalader, Wickersham & Taft) rolls out Legora to 3,300+ lawyers in 36+ offices
Pilot covered 1,300+ lawyers across 18 practice teams
13 Oct: Intake launches in Slack; Microsoft Teams, email and MCP are planned
13 Oct: Legora-Laurel partnership automatically captures time lawyers spend working in Legora
14 Oct: 30+ integrations across nine enterprise categories, plus the Sirion partnership
results.issues: The Laurel partnership is a separate 13 Oct announcement. The iManage MCP integration date could not be confirmed, so it is left out. Some integrations have been rolling out in phases since May 2026. The 'fifth-largest law firm by revenue' claim in why_it_matters was not verified.
